claims: C1 models should honor user requests
C2 honoring a user request is forbidden when it conflicts with a developer-level instruction
C3 honoring a user request is forbidden when it conflicts with a system-level instruction
C4 honoring a user request is forbidden when it conflicts with a root-level instruction

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a request from an end user, carrying user-level instruction authority

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: level A outranks level B in the instruction authority hierarchy (root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority)

concepts.name: request_level
concepts.gloss: request R is issued at instruction authority level L
concepts.inference: the clause compares a user request against instructions at other levels, so each request must carry a level for the comparison to range over

concepts.name: instruction_level
concepts.gloss: instruction I is issued at instruction authority level L
concepts.inference: the clause compares instructions at developer, system, and root levels, so each instruction must carry a level for the comparison to range over

concepts.name: conflicts_with
concepts.gloss: honoring request R would contradict what instruction I directs
concepts.inference: 'conflict' relates a request to a particular instruction it would contradict; which pairs conflict is a fact about the case

concepts.name: higher_level_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction from a level of the authority hierarchy above the user level

concepts.name: conflicts_with_higher
concepts.gloss: honoring request R would contradict some instruction issued at a level above the user level

ontology.gloss: an instruction from a level above the user level
honoring request R would contradict an instruction from a level above the user level

asserts.read_back: honoring user request % is obliged unless honoring it would conflict with a developer-, system- or root-level instruction
honoring request % is forbidden because it conflicts with instruction % from a level above the user level

closure.reason: the clause bars honoring a request only when it conflicts with a higher-level instruction; a request that conflicts with nothing is to be honored, so silence permits
